definition: An object is stored data together with metadata that describes it.
A bucket is a container for objects stored in S3.
An object key is the name used to identify an object within its bucket.
A version ID identifies a particular saved version of an object.
The current version is the most recent version returned when a request does not specify a version ID.
A noncurrent version is a saved object version that is no longer current.
A delete marker is a version that makes an object appear deleted while earlier versions can remain stored.
Multi-factor authentication requires an additional proof of identity beyond security credentials.
MFA delete requires an authentication code for permanent version deletion and bucket versioning-state changes.
Asynchronous replication copies data separately from the original write, so the copy can become available later.
A replica is an object copy that S3 creates in a replication destination bucket.
Cross-Region Replication copies matching objects to buckets in a different AWS Region.
Same-Region Replication copies matching objects to buckets in the same AWS Region.
Two-way replication uses rules in both directions so writes to either bucket can be copied to the other.
An IAM role is an identity with permissions that a trusted service or caller can assume.
A bucket policy is a resource policy that grants or denies access to a bucket and its objects.
A manifest lists the object keys and, when required, version IDs that a batch job processes.
A completion report lists batch job results for the processed objects.
A service-level agreement defines the service commitment and conditions for service credits.
Replication latency is the maximum delay in seconds between the source and destination for a replication rule.
In active-passive routing, active Regions receive requests while passive Regions do not.
In active-active routing, all configured Regions can receive requests.
Failover shifts requests away from one Region to another Region that can serve them.
A storage class determines an object storage option with particular access, placement, and billing characteristics.
An Availability Zone is an isolated location within an AWS Region.
A lifecycle rule selects objects and schedules actions such as storage transitions or expiration.
A minimum storage duration is the billed retention period that can still incur charges when data leaves a storage class early.
A restore makes archived object data readable, temporarily for Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive.
Provisioned capacity reserves capacity for Expedited retrievals from Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
Write once, read many is a storage model that protects saved data against overwriting or deletion while allowing reads.
A retention period protects an object version until its retain-until date.
Governance mode protects a version while allowing explicitly authorized requests to bypass retention.
Compliance mode prevents any account user, including root, from deleting a protected version or shortening its retention.
A legal hold protects an object version without an expiry date until an authorized caller removes it.
Encryption at rest protects data while it is stored on disk.
Server-side encryption lets S3 encrypt object data during storage and decrypt it for authorized access.
SSE-S3 is server-side object encryption with keys managed by S3.
SSE-KMS is server-side object encryption using keys managed in AWS KMS.
DSSE-KMS applies two layers of server-side encryption using KMS keys.
SSE-C is server-side encryption using a key that the caller must supply and retain.
A customer managed key is a KMS key whose policies and lifecycle are controlled by the customer.
Encryption context is additional identifying information supplied to KMS and available for policy conditions.
An ARN is an AWS identifier for a resource.
An access control list is a set of grants attached to a bucket or object.
A principal is the person, application identity, or service making an AWS request.
A VPC is a logically isolated virtual network in AWS.
A VPC endpoint enables private connectivity from a VPC to supported AWS services.
CORS uses HTTP headers to tell browsers which cross-origin requests a server permits.
An origin is the combination of a URL protocol, host, and port.
A preflight request asks whether a cross-origin method and its headers are permitted before the browser sends the actual request.
A presigned URL delegates time-limited access to a specified object operation using its signer permissions.
A bearer token grants its permitted access to anyone who possesses it while it remains valid.
A prefix is the beginning of an object key used to select related object names.
A suffix is the ending of an object key used to select matching object names.
Idempotent processing avoids repeating side effects when the same event is received more than once.
FIFO is a queue model that preserves message order within each message group.
An artifact is a file produced or consumed during a software pipeline.
Multipart upload sends an object in independent parts and assembles them when the upload is completed.
An upload ID identifies the multipart upload used to send, list, complete, or abort its parts.
A checksum is a calculated value used to detect whether data changed during transfer or storage.
An ETag is an object content identifier that is an MD5 digest only for certain upload and encryption combinations.
MD5 is a digest algorithm that produces a value used to compare data content.
An edge location is a network entry point close to users that can route accelerated uploads toward S3.
CSV is a text report format whose values are separated by commas.
ORC is a column-oriented data format supported by S3 Inventory.
Parquet is a column-oriented data format supported by S3 Inventory.
A data event records resource activity such as reading or writing an S3 object.
Signature Version 4 adds authentication information to AWS API requests.
